drhp.business: The Company manufactures and sells denim fabrics and cotton yarn/textured yarn in domestic and international markets, with an integrated production operation in Rajasthan. It also trades Denim Garments under its own consumer brand, "Manomay – India's First Denim CoreWear Brand," and operates an e-commerce platform for denim formal pants, jeans, shorts, cargos and lowers.
drhp.end_markets: Domestic India (major cities including New Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Ahmadabad, Ludhiana, Bhilwara, Bangalore)|South America|Middle East|Asia|18+ overseas markets
drhp.expansion: The Company has undertaken a forward integration initiative into denim apparel under its own consumer brand "Manomay – India's First Denim CoreWear Brand" with a soft-launched e-commerce platform (02.05.2025), shifting from a fabric manufacturer to a vertically integrated fibre-to-fashion entity. In 2025, additional spindles (864) were installed at the spinning unit to enhance existing capacity. In 2024, the Company commenced commercial production of cotton yarn at its spinning plant in Undawa, Tehsil Gangrar, Chittorgarh. Earlier, the Company installed new Tsudakoma Brand Automatic Shuttleless ZAX001NEO Air Jet Looms (36 sets) at the Denim plant, increasing production capacity by 33% while removing 36 old looms, and applied for a 1.1 MW captive Solar PV power project at the Denim plant site (approved 06.07.2022 under the Rajasthan Solar Energy Policy, 2019).

litigation.note: No significant or material orders passed by regulators, courts, or tribunals impacting going-concern status during the year, per Board's Report.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Rising disposable incomes and urbanisation among the Indian middle class are expected to drive demand for branded/premium denim products.
- Low per-capita consumption of denim in India (roughly 0.4 pairs per person annually) is cited as headroom for domestic expansion.
- India's position as one of the fastest-growing major denim sectors in the Asia-Pacific region and growing demand for Indian-made denim in the US and Europe support export growth.
- Government policy tailwinds for the textile sector (Make in India, PLI Scheme, PM MITRA Park Scheme, MEIS, RoDTEP) support competitiveness and exports.
- India's cotton production advantage (world's largest producer, high-quality long-staple cotton) supports raw-material availability and export competitiveness.
- Sustainability and traceability mandates (e.g., EU environmental compliance frameworks) are shaping global buyer requirements and are being addressed through cleaner production, circularity and responsible sourcing efforts.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The Company has undertaken a forward integration initiative into denim apparel under its own consumer brand "Manomay – India's First Denim CoreWear Brand" with a soft-launched e-commerce platform (02.05.2025), shifting from a fabric manufacturer to a vertically integrated fibre-to-fashion entity. In 2025, additional spindles (864) were installed at the spinning unit to enhance existing capacity. In 2024, the Company commenced commercial production of cotton yarn at its spinning plant in Undawa, Tehsil Gangrar, Chittorgarh. Earlier, the Company installed new Tsudakoma Brand Automatic Shuttleless ZAX001NEO Air Jet Looms (36 sets) at the Denim plant, increasing production capacity by 33% while removing 36 old looms, and applied for a 1.1 MW captive Solar PV power project at the Denim plant site (approved 06.07.2022 under the Rajasthan Solar Energy Policy, 2019).

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- integration: Integrated Denim and Spinning production facility allowing all operations in-house — evidence: "an integrated facility, allowing us to carry out all operations in-house"
- distribution: Existing B2B relationships with repeat-order traders — evidence: "our existing client being traders provides us repeated orders"
- distribution: Global presence across 18+ overseas markets with an agent/dealer network — evidence: "exports our denim to 18+ countries worldwide"

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Volatility in the prices of cotton and transportation costs could impede business profits and prospects.
- Denim and Spinning production facilities are vulnerable to machinery unavailability, breakdown or obsolescence, disruption in power supplies, performance below projected efficiency, and labor disputes; replacement parts for such machinery may not always be available.
- The Company has expanded into international markets and is vulnerable to fluctuations in the exchange rate between the Rupee and other currencies, which could have a major unfavorable effect on operating results and financial condition.
- The Company faces competition from both organized and unorganized textile companies, including numerous major corporations, which could negatively impact business operations and financial condition.
- A fall in revenue, rising competition, or change in demand from key clients may have a detrimental effect on the Company's ability to retain them.
- The Company does not have an offshore office or company location to manage its export operations, which may limit its ability to capitalize on opportunities in the evolving worldwide garment market in a timely manner.
- Risk of loss from inadequate or failed internal processes, people and systems, or external events such as economic/market conditions, intense local and international competition, and new entrants into textile markets.
- Products are influenced by consumer expectations, customer preferences, and fashion trends; failure to maintain product quality standards may impact the business.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Diversification of product portfolio, addition of new capacities, and exploring new geographies as the next phase of growth.
- Forward integration from a leading denim fabric manufacturer into a vertically integrated fibre-to-fashion entity via the Manomay CoreWear brand and e-commerce platform, enhancing value capture across the supply chain.
- Continued modernisation of spinning and denim fabric facilities to gain efficiency and product sophistication.
- Seeking enduring relationships with an extensive network of agents and dealers in India and across the world, with a strong reputation among Denim fabric manufacturers in key markets such as Latin America.
- Offering superior, differentiated Denim (Cotton) products aligned with emerging fashion trends and customer needs, through innovative, cost-effective and sustainable solutions and total quality management.
